Unless you're a fucking spastic who wouldn't be trusted to hold the kitchen knives, the whole making hamburger of your face thing isn't really an issue.

The trick is always have a good lather on where you're shaving (never shave without it), keep a good angle, and don't force the blade if you meet resistance.

If there's a shaving shop near you, go ask them. They'll generally be more than happy to show you what to do.

The fake ones are called shavettes. They are a great transition from DE safety razors because you can snap the DE blades in half.

It'll take a week to feel comfortable shaving and a month to get good at it. The keys are a firm grip on the razor, going slow, light pressure, go slow, and shave at a low angle. You will cut yourself a few times, but as long as you're going slow with light pressure, the cuts won't be the bad.

It doesn't take long to learn, and little knicks can happen to anyone. I can't get my whole face shaved with a single blade on those "fake straights". I think they're best for a barber to use to line up your neckline etc. Anything counts as practice, though.

If you're just starting out, look for razors with a rounded outer blade edge. Only shave with or across the grain until you're more skilled and never upwards under your nose.
